subject: Materials Science
title: Rockwell and Vickers Hardness
description: A quick, practical guide to Rockwell and Vickers Hardness.

hook.text: The Brinell test is slow — Rockwell gives a hardness number in seconds on a dial.

buildup.text: Rockwell measures depth of indentation under load — the dial reads hardness directly, no microscope needed.

discovery.text: Vickers uses a diamond pyramid and measures the diagonal of the indent — works on everything from lead to ceramics.

twist.text: Rockwell has different scales (A, B, C) for different materials — you can't compare across scales.

climax.text: HRC 60 means a file won't scratch it — that's hardened tool steel or a razor blade.

punchline.text: Different tests, same question — how hard is it to dent?

quiz.question: What advantage does Rockwell testing have over Brinell?
options: It gives a direct readout without microscopic measurement
